text: Ever wondered why a piece of bread starts to taste sweet if you keep it in your mouth long enough? Something in your saliva is cutting starch into sugar, right there, while the cells of your tongue sit in the same liquid untouched. That something is an enzyme. Your body runs thousands of reactions at once, at body temperature, and left to themselves many would be far too slow to keep you alive. Enzymes speed particular reactions by acting on suitable substrates. How, and where, is this lesson.
